relations.evidence: Kidwell received her bachelor's degree in 1963.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.evidence: She earned her master's in 1966 from OU.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.evidence: She finally received her Ph.D from the University of Oklahoma in 1970.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.evidence: Kidwell began to teach American Indian studies in 1970 at Haskell Indian Junior College (now Haskell Indian Nations University). She worked at Haskell for two years

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.evidence: until she left to be an associate professor at the University of California at Berkeley where she worked until 1993.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.evidence: In 1980, she was a visiting scholar and associate professor at Dartmouth College.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.object: National Museum of the American Indian
relations.evidence: After Berkeley, she took her career in a new direction as the assistant director for cultural resources at the National Museum of the American Indian.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.role: director of the Native American studies program
relations.evidence: In 1995, she chose a tenured position at the University of Oklahoma as the director of the Native American studies program.

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.evidence: In 2007, Kidwell started the American Indian Center (AIC) at the University of North Carolina (UNC).

relations.subject: Clara Sue Kidwell
relations.object: American Indian Center (AIC) at the University of North Carolina
relations.evidence: Kidwell retired from her position as director of AIC in June 2011.
